questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and we are already given the coefficients ${a}_{0}$ and ${a}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼-\frac{13}{3}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{64(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, notice that 

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-2,2),$

- continuous on $[-2,2),$ and

- satisfies $F(-2)=F(2),$ if we extend the value at $x=2$ using the formula $F(x)=-4{x}^{2}+1.$

Therefore, the $4$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{continuous}$ and $\text{piecewise smooth}$ on $R,$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4{x}^{2}+1) & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{13}{3})+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{64(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\ -8x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{64(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\ -8x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-32(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\ -8x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{32(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=\pi $ and we are already given the coefficients ${a}_{0}$ and ${a}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼3+\frac{7{\pi }^{2}}{6}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{14(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Now, notice that 

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-\pi ,\pi ),$

- continuous on $[-\pi ,\pi ),$ and

- satisfies $F(-\pi )=F(\pi ),$ if we extend the value at $x=\pi $ using the formula $F(x)=\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+3.$

Therefore, the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{continuous}$ and $\text{piecewise smooth}$ on $R,$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+3) & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3+\frac{7{\pi }^{2}}{6})+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{14(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)) \\ 7x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{14(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\cdot (-n\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)) \\ 7x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-14(-1)^{n}}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx) \\ 7x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{14(-1)^{n+1}}{n}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$
